successors.name: Grand Principality of Moscow
successors.text: the Vladimir core and the appanages that Cliopatria's Moscow shape holds by 1395 (the 1375 shape without the 1395 shape), plus the capital

successors.name: Principality of Yaroslavl
successors.text: the land round Yaroslavl that the 1375 and 1395 shapes share (Yaroslavl Oblast, 84 cells) without the Rostov and Uglich-Bezhetsk discs; 'the lands around Yaroslavl on both banks of the Volga River'…

successors.name: Principality of Rostov
successors.text: the land round Rostov the Great that the 1375 and 1395 shapes share (12 cells); the disc is 40 km of mine, the pages give no extent

successors.name: Principality of Uglich
successors.text: the land round Uglich and Bezhetsk that the 1375 and 1395 shapes share (19 cells), the appanage of Andrey Bolshoy in Vasily II's will; the discs are 40 km of mine, the pages give no extent

rulers.name: Dmitry of Tver, Fearsome Eyes (Dmitry I)

ledger.x: 1294: the Grand Principality of Vladimir, 'fragmented into over a dozen appanages' and ruled by a prince whom the khan appoints, is drawn again on its capital Vladimir.
1294: the Grand Principality of Vladimir is a vassal of the Horde, its grand prince appointed by the khan.
1305: Pereslavl-Zalessky and its neighbours pass to Moscow.
1333: a strip of the Mologa country passes to Moscow.
1344: Galich, Kostroma and the Vologda country pass to Moscow.

1389: the grand principality ends as a state, and with it this dossier's vassal relation to the Horde; the land stays tributary through Moscow and the appanages (footnote, 1389: 'the grand prince was invested by the envoy of the Mongol khan'). golden-horde.json has the vassal_end of this slug in 1480: it…
1389: the throne of Vladimir is permanently united with Moscow's, and the core of the grand principality (Vladimir and the appanages Moscow already holds) passes to the Grand Principality of Moscow.
1389: the Yaroslavl lands stay outside Moscow as the Principality of Yaroslavl.
1389: the Rostov lands stay outside Moscow as the Principality of Rostov, absorbed by Moscow in 1474.
1389: the Uglich and Bezhetsk lands stay outside Moscow's own domain.

1389: the southern Vologda country and the other cells of the 1395 shape (not Yaroslavl, Rostov, Uglich or Bezhetsk) are in no Vladimir-Suzdal hand after the dissolution, but the pages opened name no holder for them until Vasily II's will gave 'Andrey Menshoy...
1389: the Grand Principality of Vladimir ends as a separate state.

wars.name: Struggle between Moscow and Tver for the grand princedom of Vladimir
wars.outcome: Moscow prevailed: Ivan I became sole grand prince in 1331, the throne was united with Moscow's for good by 1389, and Tver became Dmitry's junior ('elder brother') in 1375.

wars.name: Tver Uprising of 1327
wars.outcome: Tver's rising of 15 August 1327 was crushed by a Mongol force led by Ivan of Moscow and Alexander of Suzdal; in 1328 Ozbeg divided the grand principality between Alexander of Suzdal and Ivan I of Moscow, and on Alexander's death in 1331 Ivan was sole grand…
